facts_and_goals: I have a full-time job and evening classes. I have slept poorly this week. My manager offered an optional weekend shift; declining will not affect my job. The extra pay would be nice but is not needed for bills. I want to protect my study time and avoid overcommitting.

relevant_considerations.text: The shift is optional and declining has no job penalty.
Sleep and study time are already strained.
The pay is useful but not essential.

facts_and_goals: I am struggling to practice a language consistently. A free weekly conversation group meets nearby at a time when I am normally free. It accepts beginners and I can leave after one session. I want more speaking practice but feel nervous about attending.

relevant_considerations.text: The trial is free and reversible.
Speaking practice matches the stated goal.
Initial nervousness and group fit still matter.

facts_and_goals: A friend canceled two plans at short notice this month. One cancellation was due to a family problem; I do not know the reason for the other. We usually get along and have not discussed how cancellations affect me. I want a reliable friendship without assuming bad intentions.
option_a: raise the cancellations in a conversation
option_b: let it go without discussing it

relevant_considerations.text: There may be missing context for the second cancellation.
A calm conversation can address reliability without assuming motives.
Consider whether this is a persistent pattern.

facts_and_goals: My three-year-old vacuum has a worn hose. A compatible replacement hose costs 20 units and has a return policy. A new vacuum costs 250 units. The motor still works well. I want reliable cleaning while avoiding unnecessary spending.

relevant_considerations.text: The repair is much cheaper and returnable.
Confirm that the hose is compatible.
